summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma s/p TACE was admitted for severe nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Initial concern for infection or bowel ischemia was ruled out with imaging and labs. A CT scan showed a new hypodense lesion in the liver corresponding to the recent TACE site, consistent with post-TACE inflammation. Her symptoms improved with supportive care, including IV fluids, anti-nausea medications, and pain control. She was restarted on her liver medications, including lactulose and spironolactone, and received prophylactic diazepam due to mild alcohol withdrawal symptoms. Her condition stabilized, she advanced to a regular diet, and was discharged home in improved condition with follow-up arranged with her hepatologist and primary care provider.
